regions.name: Central Sahel
regions.why: A semi-arid belt that lived a great drought in the 1970s–80s.

T2M.label: Air temperature
T2M.simple: How warm the air is 2 metres above the ground — what a thermometer in the shade shows.

TS.label: Surface temperature
TS.simple: The temperature of the surface itself — soil, rock, sea water or ice — which can be much hotter or colder than the air above it.

PRECTOTCORR.label: Precipitation
PRECTOTCORR.simple: How much rain and snow falls, in millimetres of water per day (1 mm on one square metre is one litre). MERRA-2 corrects its model rain with rain gauges and satellite observations.

GWETROOT.label: Root-zone soil wetness
GWETROOT.simple: How wet the soil is where plant roots drink (roughly the top metre): 0 % is bone dry, 100 % is completely soaked.

EVLAND.label: Evaporation from land
EVLAND.simple: Water rising from the land into the air — from wet soil, lakes and plant leaves (transpiration) — in millimetres per day.

RH2M.label: Relative humidity
RH2M.simple: How close the air is to being saturated with water vapour: at 100 % it cannot hold more and dew or fog forms.

TQV.label: Water vapour in the air column
TQV.simple: All the water vapour above a spot, from the ground to the top of the atmosphere — the millimetres of water you would get if it all rained out at once.

SLP.label: Sea-level pressure
SLP.simple: The weight of the air above a spot, as if measured at sea level (about 1013 hPa on average): low pressure brings storms, high pressure fair weather.

WS10M.label: Wind speed
WS10M.simple: How fast the wind blows 10 metres above the ground (10 m/s is 36 km/h).

TROPT.label: Tropopause temperature
TROPT.simple: The temperature at the tropopause, the ceiling of the weather layer of the atmosphere: about 8 km up near the poles and 17 km up in the tropics.

links.text: Air temperature and Surface temperature leave their norm in the same months, the same way: 104 times, where chance at the same moment of the record would give 20 (p = 4e-64; z = 25.7 against the same reading with one of them moved 1 to 5 years, beyond the shared trend and the persistence of each). story.text: Root-zone soil wetness — Central Sahel: +0.62 % per decade (95 % range +0.406 to +0.88). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 3.5e-07, t-test p = 2.5e-06. Eva: Since 2011, 81 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Evaporation from land — Central Sahel: +0.06 mm/day per decade (95 % range +0.0363 to +0.0911). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 6.2e-05, t-test p = 4.5e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 67 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Relative humidity — Central Sahel: +0.88 % per decade (95 % range +0.41 to +1.31). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.0012, t-test p = 0.0028. Eva: Since 2011, 67 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Water vapour in the air column — Central Sahel: +0.54 kg/m² per decade (95 % range +0.246 to +0.807). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.00074, t-test p = 0.0039. Eva: Since 2011, 69 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Wind speed — Central Sahel: -0.04 m/s per decade (95 % range -0.0644 to -0.0254). Significant falling trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.00012, t-test p = 4.5e-05. Eva: Since 2011, 66 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Air temperature — Central Sahel: +0.14 °C per decade (95 % range +0.0329 to +0.262). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.013, t-test p = 0.0041. Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 53 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Surface temperature — Central Sahel: +0.14 °C per decade (95 % range +0.00478 to +0.262). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 0.043, t-test p = 0.015. Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 52 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Precipitation — Central Sahel: +0.09 mm/day per decade (95 % range +0.0508 to +0.135). Significant rising trend: both tests agree at the 95 % level. Mann-Kendall p = 9e-05, t-test p = 2.5e-05. Eva: Since 2011, months come out above Eva's expectation 57 % of the time: not clearly different from her 1981–2010 norm.

Sea-level pressure — Central Sahel: +0.07 hPa per decade (95 % range +0.00292 to +0.158). A rising trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.039, t-test p = 0.098. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 67 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 70 % of months came out higher than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.

Tropopause temperature — Central Sahel: -0.30 °C per decade (95 % range -0.635 to +0.0409). A falling trend that only one test (or only the 90 % level) supports. Mann-Kendall p = 0.075, t-test p = 0.062. With this much natural variability, a trend of this size needs about 33 years of data to stand out (45 so far). Eva: Since 2011, 62 % of months came out lower than Eva's norm expected from their neighbours (50 % if nothing had changed): the dynamic has left the norm she learned in 1981–2010.
